coverage_rows.canon_label: Cleanup Action Semantics
exact_items: Historical lane/worktree record must survive archive, prune, and remove
archive = retire from active use while preserving enough identity/metadata/lineage for historical browsing
prune = cleanup-oriented action for items already policy-eligible; narrower than generic remove and typically scoped to obviously stale/orphaned/live-no-longer-needed worktrees
recover = attempt to restore or reconcile a suspect/orphaned/conflicted worktree into safe known state
remove = explicit destructive removal of live worktree backing after confirmation and eligibility checks

coverage_rows.canon_label: Cleanup Eligibility Gating
exact_items: Checks before archive/prune/remove: no active-run ownership, no unresolved blocked recovery requiring that exact worktree, no required safe-point restore targeting that worktree/baseline, no unresolved conflict workflow user still needs, no newer lineage operation depending on that lane/worktree still being live

coverage_rows.canon_label: Cleanup Trigger Conditions
exact_items: Good candidate transitions into cleanup_eligible: lane/package complete and no retention reason remains, superseded by graph patch and no unresolved recovery depends on it, revoked/reopened flow leaves old lane/worktree no longer needed live, recovery completed and old broken backing no longer needed

Good candidate transitions into retained instead of immediate cleanup: recent completion pending review/promotion, weak integration still under investigation, unresolved concern or corroboration tied to outputs from that lane, manual operator retention

coverage_rows.canon_label: Command Palette Exposure Policy
exact_items: Palette-allowed but guarded: recover / retry / approve / decline / replan / restore / cleanup actions with canonical runtime semantics and confirmation rules
Palette-discouraged or hidden by default: broad destructive bulk mutations with ambiguous target sets

Palette-friendly: open/focus tab, jump to run/seam/package/node/lane/concern/review/patch/recovery object, open inspector/detail/history/ledger/evidence context, run search routes, low-risk view and filter commands

review should persist scope, review type, actor linkage, verdict/severity/blocking, findings, evidence, and timestamps

exact_items: merge: several concern records collapse into surviving concern with lineage refs from old ones
newer concern should carry lineage back to prior ids
old concern ids remain queryable in Ledger/History after merge/split/supersession
resolution_kind candidates: fixed, accepted_risk, superseded, merged, split, invalidated, obsoleted_by_patch, obsoleted_by_recovery
split: one concern reframed into multiple precise concerns; original resolves with resolution_kind=split
superseded: concern replaced by newer concern or broader canonical object framing

coverage_rows.canon_label: Concern source-update and interaction with other families
exact_items: blocked episodes can: reference concern when concern becomes execution-blocking; should not be replaced by concern record
corroboration can: validate concern, downgrade to advisory/minor, leave unresolved minority concern
do not merge automatically just because summaries look similar; use source/scope/category/lineage-aware heuristics or explicit governance action
graph patch can: resolve concern, obsolete concern, split into more precise post-patch concerns
recovery can: resolve concern, create follow-on concern if recovery exposes new issue
repeated sightings of same underlying issue should usually update existing concern rather than minting duplicates
review findings may nominate or update concerns but review record remains distinct
